doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Merv Griffin as boss and the Joe Pass story
summary: Griffin let him travel freely; stories about hiring Jim Hall and defending Joe Pass.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well nine years on Merv Griffin, you know.

Well that wasn’t anything, but it kept me off the streets. Because everything faded at that time. Everything, the bottom fell out. And now — at least parts of Europe, I used to go over there every now and then, and take off a week here and take off a — he was very liberal about that. Very nice about it. You can go anywhere or take off anytime you want, go anywhere you want. The job is yours when you come back. So that’s the kind of a guy he was.
Yeah, you can come back, do anything you want. I don’t care what you do. Just get a competent guy you know. So it was great.

Oh, yeah, yeah. We had a good band, good guys in the bands though. And he wanted all- star bands, he did. Mundell Lowe left he says, “I’ve got a great guitar player for him, but he doesn’t have any hair.” He wants all young looking guys. So Danny Stiles says, “this guy’s the best.” He brought him the Down Beat polls, and he says, “Well this guy won all the polls, let me see what he looks like.” He brought him in it was Jim Hall. And he says, “Here’s our new guitar, Jim Hall, come on out here, let’s do a tune.” So he and them just did a tune. He says, “You’re hired.” So another time came up, the band leader was always trying to get rid of some of the stars and get his guys on there see, like get rid of me and get his kid drummer on there. So one time out in L.A. we were out there and he wanted to get this other guitar player from The Tonight Show on there, who happens to be very good, but Herbie Ellis got Joe Pass to come in there. And so Herbie and I went out to eat one night after Joe had done the job, and Herbie says, “You know, Jake, Mort says Merv hated this guy because he had no hair.” He was a bald headed guy. He said, “I just don’t know what to do, gez, now Mort’s mad at me and he wants to get his guy on there.” I says, “Well if that’s what he wants to do, you’re listening to Mort, let’s go to the source.” He says, “Oh we can’t talk to Merv.” I says, “Who can’t talk to Merv? Come on.” And we left the Brown Derby and we went up backstage and rapped on the door and Merv was sitting right by the door and he opened it up and he was in a conference with about twelve guys. He says, “Hey Jake how you doin’? When’d you get back?” I says, “Just today, I just had supper with Herbie.” He says, “What’s this you don’t like that guitar player he sent to me the other night? Joe Pass?” “Joe Pass? What do you mean? He’s better than you are, Herbie.” He says, “You better be careful who you send in here from now on. That guy’s the greatest.” I said, “See? This guy was lying all the time.” See? Herbie says, “Jesus. Always go to the top.” Well word got around that somebody was

dissatisfied or said that he was dissatisfied with him. “You come to me when you’ve got something to ask me, man. Don’t ask somebody else.” That’s how he was. He was very good at that. Very good at that. Now don’t fool with him, because he’ll chop your head off. But he’d stick right by you you know. If he’s your enemy you’d better leave, you’d better leave. No use hanging around.
